title: Formalize the generalized Stokes theorem: FTC as a special case

problemStatement.formal: ∫_M dω = ∫_{∂M} ω, with M=[a,b] giving FTC: ∫_a^b F'dx = F(b)-F(a)
problemStatement.plain: Formalize the generalized Stokes theorem showing FTC (1D), Green's theorem (2D), classical Stokes' theorem, and the divergence theorem as special cases of ∫_M dω = ∫_{∂M} ω.
whyMatters: Unifies all fundamental integral theorems of calculus
Connects analysis (FTC), topology (de Rham cohomology), and algebra (exterior calculus)
Foundation for modern differential geometry and physics

proven: Poincare lemma in 1D: every continuous 1-form is exact
Antiderivative uniqueness: two antiderivatives differ by a constant
de Rham cohomology: H^0(R) = R, H^1(R) = 0
open: d^2 = 0 (Clairaut) — stated, needs Mathlib bridge for iteratedFDeriv
Green's theorem in Stokes form — stated, full proof in GreensTheoremOQ01
General Stokes theorem on manifolds with boundary
knownResults.goal: Complete formalization of the Stokes hierarchy with proved d^2=0
